papers.rationale: Adaptable dexterous skill learning is central; baseline comparisons, generalization, cross-simulator transfer, and real-world deployment are demonstrated.
Studies general manipulation and textual memory rather than specified filters; comparative benchmarks and real-world task improvements are reported.
Fleet memory supports operational understanding incidentally related to navigation; validation establishes decoder equivalence, without comparative autonomy evaluation.
Visuotactile world modeling targets general manipulation rather than specified filters; comparative real-world policy improvements are measured across four tasks.
Post-trains high-level task planners rather than motion planners; comparative LIBERO-PRO simulation results show substantial success improvements.
Scene reconstruction supports general manipulation simulation rather than specified filters; comparative reconstruction and policy-outcome prediction evaluations are described.
Predictive indoor exploration directly addresses navigation; comparative floor-plan and real-SLAM environment evaluations demonstrate exploration improvements.
Humanoid contact interaction policies centrally address whole-body control; comparative modeling evaluations and onboard hardware demonstrations are reported.
Humanoid whole-body tracking is central; extensive comparative benchmarks, scaling across motions, and physical humanoid transfer demonstrate generalization.
Dynamics-aware humanoid retargeting directly supports whole-body control; comparative tracking evaluations and sim-to-real transfer are demonstrated.
Lunar rover simulation directly supports navigation development; shadow and stereo validation are reported without comparative navigation evaluation.
Tactile control addresses general contact-rich manipulation, without dexterous-hand or other filter contributions; comparative task success and tactile ablations are reported.
Industrial mobile robot navigation is central; comparative onboard real-world benchmarks quantify success, efficiency, and sim-to-real improvements.
Stage-aware manipulation includes dexterous-hand and humanoid embodiments; comparative experiments and explicit transfer across architectures and embodiments support generalization.
Benchmarks contextual task-plan safety rather than robot motion planning; comparative dataset evaluation covers nine language models.
Navigation among movable obstacles is central; comparative simulation and real-robot trials demonstrate faster planning and higher success.
Elastic-arm trajectory tracking does not directly address specified filters; simulations and hardware experiments explicitly demonstrate cross-trajectory adaptation under modeling mismatches.
Direct robot control evaluation examines motion feasibility and coordinated motion; comparative simulation benchmarks and qualitative hardware corroboration are reported.
Secure communication supports mapping and heading consensus incidentally related to navigation; hardware and scaling demonstrations lack stated comparative evaluation.
Hazard-responsive driving trajectory generation directly addresses motion planning; comparative simulated counterfactuals, replay, and closed-loop braking evaluations demonstrate improvements.
Latent task-plan selection incidentally covers routes, without explicit motion-planning contribution; comparative simulation experiments quantify steering improvements.
Predictive representations target general manipulation rather than specified filters; comparative real-world results and transfer across policy architectures are demonstrated.
Rover thermal engineering is unrelated to specified autonomy filters; thermal simulations are verified by a vacuum thermal-balance experiment.
Single-step world-action prediction targets general manipulation rather than specified filters; comparative simulation and real-world task advantages are reported.
Runtime task grounding and grasp recovery address general manipulation rather than specified filters; comparative LIBERO-PRO evaluation covers multiple policy backbones.
